purpose: Student-facing expected direct notebook delivery; not a guarantee of provider behavior.
shortCopy: Your AI should check the material and give you the finished notebook JSON, named after the notebook. Ask for a draft first only if you want one.
expandedCopy: Use a normal chat with your material; projects are optional. The AI should explain the ideas clearly, check sources and practice, and deliver the final file without a required approval conversation. It should ask only for essential missing information and briefly note important gaps or changes. These are expected behaviors, not guarantees.
revisionCopy: To update a notebook, save your edits and give your AI the current JSON plus new material. It should preserve unaffected content and deliver the checked revised JSON with a short account of changes. You review and accept the update separately in the app.
revisionLimits: Current JSON includes saved content and retained sources, not unsaved edits, separate notes or practice progress. Your app controls final acceptance, history and study records; the AI cannot claim to save or transfer them.
materialsCopy: Upload supported files or paste text directly in your AI chat. For a question, handwriting or figure that is unclear or missing from document extraction, add a clear image with its full setup and diagram. Your AI should identify what it actually read and ask only about consequential gaps.
intakeCopy: If you are sending several batches, tell your AI when you are done. It should track what arrived and what it actually read, then check and deliver the notebook.
standardizationCopy: Your AI should verify the course and scope, inspect the available material, explain the ideas and preserve source gaps and saved edits. It should deliver a complete titled file and state actual check limits. A hosted chat cannot guarantee where your browser saves it; an authorized local assistant can save it in Downloads without overwriting existing files.
visualsCopy: Your AI should inspect the supplied visual material, keep useful original figures with their source context, and provide any image files needed with the JSON. Practice must show its necessary neutral setup or figure before you try it; missing images stay explicit.
